title: Column- and object-level security: GRANTs that keep salary out of reach
objective_text: Write the GRANT SELECT plan for three roles on a warehouse, using column-level security to hide pay columns and no grant at all to keep a whole table out of reach.
scenario: The HR warehouse has an Employees table and a SalaryHistory table. Managers, analysts and a payroll app each read it through the SQL analytics endpoint. None of them has a role in the workspace, so what they read is exactly what you grant.
engine_label: A model of a warehouse's GRANT SELECT statements, checked on this PC
verifies: Your grants give each role the tables and columns it needs and no more, with Salary, BankAccount and SalaryHistory out of the analysts' reach, checked against a model on this PC.
does_not_verify: That the statements run in a Fabric Warehouse: no T-SQL runs here. In Fabric the analysts' grant is GRANT SELECT ON dbo.Employees(EmployeeID, FullName, Department, Email, HireDate) TO [Analysts].
DENY, and how DENY and GRANT combine.
Workspace Admins, Members and Contributors, whose roles reach all data whatever the grants say.

expected.description: HRManagers: * on both tables. Analysts: five named columns of Employees, no SalaryHistory. PayrollApp: EmployeeID, Salary and BankAccount of Employees only.

validation.fail: Analysts can still read pay data, or can't read what their reports need.
validation.pass: Analysts read Employees without Salary or BankAccount, and nothing in SalaryHistory.

rules.why: SELECT on the whole table would include Salary and BankAccount; list the columns instead.
No grant on the table at all is object-level security: the whole table is out of reach.

validation.fail: PayrollApp gets more, or less, than its three columns.
validation.pass: PayrollApp reads exactly EmployeeID, Salary and BankAccount.
HRManagers read both tables in full.

hints: Column-level security is a GRANT SELECT that lists columns. A column left out of the list can't be selected.
To keep a role out of a whole table, give it no grant on that table.
Check PayrollApp as carefully as Analysts: least privilege applies to apps too.
explanation: Column-level security in a Fabric Warehouse is a GRANT SELECT that names the columns a user or role may read. A query that touches any other column fails, and so does SELECT *. Listing the five safe columns keeps pay data from analysts without a second table or view. A table a role has no grant on is out of its reach entirely, which is how SalaryHistory stays hidden. Grant to roles rather than to individuals: it's easier to manage.
review_notes: Checked on Learn 2026-11-06 (column-level-security): CLS is applied with GRANT on listed columns, roles are preferred to individuals, and the page's example shows SELECT * failing with Msg 230 on the column not granted.
DENY is left out because its behaviour wasn't checked against a source in this batch.
